messages:
alex: FYI nightly e2e perf gate turned red on longseq p99 at 03:12 UTC, started right after the runtime merge (sha: 5b8c2f7). failing job: nightly-e2e-longseq-2026-03-16.
jyoti: ugh. can someone paste the perf summary/dashboard link?
alex: https://dash.redwood.example/perf/builds/2467 — p99 jumped from 120ms -> 380ms for longseq. throughput steady but latency tail spiked. shipping log snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T03:11:45Z] model_infer: kv_cache_miss=0.03 lat=2.1ms token
[2026-03-16T03:12:01Z] attention_kern: p99=380.2ms
[2026-03-16T03:12:01Z] runner: batch_size=8 seq=2048
``` 
marc: cc @taylor any recent scheduler/compilation changes in that merge? I remember you touched kernel selection.
taylor: yep i merged the kernel selector PR yesterday that adds a small heuristic for seq>1024. It should favor tiled matmul kernels. I did a quick canary and it looked fine. will dig in.
sophie: can we try a quick rerun before triaging? sometimes it's flaky. i'll kick a rerun in ~2m.
ci-bot: rerun requested by sophie — job nightly-e2e-longseq-2467 requeued (id: 2467-r2)
alex: thanks. if rerun is green we can chalk it to noise. if it stays red, we should bisect the runtime PR vs previous deploy.
jyoti: rerun started.
marc: another datapoint: canary region (canary-1) p95 stayed around baseline earlier today, only nightly is red — maybe it's scale/queue interaction.
taylor: if it's scale-sensitive maybe the tiled kernel has a perf cliff at certain batch shapes. i'll add logs to capture kernel choices.
sophie: rerun finished — still red. p99 372ms. not noise.
alex: ok bisect time. @taylor can you bisect between before/after your selector? smallest useful range is the selector PR + last two related commits.
taylor: will do. also going to revert the selector in a canary branch and run the smoke e2e locally.
marc: i can run the sherlock bench across commits if you want — will take ~30m.
jyoti: also opening a quick experiment: force older kernel via env `USE_KERNEL=tiled_v1` vs `tiled_v0` to confirm regression.
alex: plan: 1) taylor bisects and tries revert canary 2) marc runs sherlock for confirmation 3) jyoti runs kernel-forcing experiment 4) sophie keeps the reruns and watches alerting. update here with commit ranges and results. :thumbsup:
taylor: starting bisect now, will post the first failing commit and logs in this thread.
